headings.text: Four kinds of roof emergency, one response
headings.excerpt: Whatever the cause, the first visit has the same goal: no more water in the building tonight. The permanent repair comes next, in daylight, with the right materials.

headings.text: A family at 2 a.m. and a property manager with forty tenants
headings.excerpt: The same line, the same crews, a different plan. A home needs the water stopped and the family reassured. A building needs the water stopped, tenants informed, the loading dock kept open and a report in the owner's inbox

headings.text: Leaks, storm damage, trees, ice dams
headings.excerpt: We tarp or flash the same day where the weather allows, trace the leak from inside the attic rather than guessing from the ground, and give you a written repair proposal with photos before anything permanent is done. If

headings.text: Retail, warehouses, condos, care facilities, schools
headings.excerpt: One call reaches a crew that has done this on flat, metal and shingle roofs across the state. We stabilize the roof, protect stock and equipment, keep entrances and docks usable, write up the damage for your insurer and

headings.text: What the emergency crew does on arrival
headings.excerpt: The truck carries what an emergency usually needs: tarps, battens, temporary flashing, sealants, plywood, snow tools, pumps. The aim is a dry building tonight and a clear picture of what the permanent fix is.

headings.text: Tarp and dry-in shingle, slate, tile
headings.excerpt: What: heavy tarps battened down over the damage, or a synthetic underlayment dry-in on exposed decking. Why: stops the water immediately and keeps the deck from soaking while the repair is planned.

headings.text: Leak tracing from the attic side
headings.excerpt: What: we find where the water enters, not just where it shows; chimney flashing, pipe boots, valleys and skylights are the usual culprits. Why: a patch on the stain is a second visit waiting to happen.

headings.text: Temporary flashing and sealing penetrations, walls, curbs
headings.excerpt: What: temporary metal and sealant at the failed detail so the building stays dry until the proper flashing is rebuilt. Why: most leaks are a detail, and a detail can be made safe in an hour.

headings.text: Flat roof emergency patching EPDM, TPO, mod-bit
headings.excerpt: What: membrane patches, seam reseal, drain and scupper clearing, water pumped off a ponding roof. Why: on a flat roof, a blocked drain alone can bring a ceiling down.

headings.text: Snow and ice relief steaming, removal, load relief
headings.excerpt: What: ice dams opened with steam, not hammers; snow removed from overloaded flat roofs and eaves; channels cut so meltwater drains. Why: ice dams push water uphill under shingles; wet snow on a flat roof is a structural

headings.text: Documentation for you and your insurer
headings.excerpt: What: photos before and after, a written description of the damage and its cause, and a scope of the permanent repair. Why: claims are won on documentation; we have been doing this for insurers for thirty years.

headings.text: What you see, and whether it can wait until morning
headings.excerpt: Some things need a crew tonight. Some are a next-day appointment and we will tell you so honestly, because an emergency call-out costs more than a scheduled one.
Emergency: yes. Catch the water, relieve a bulging ceiling with a small hole, call us. We do: trace the entry point, tarp or flash the same day, schedule the permanent repair.
